rationale.conceptual: Periodic Hartree-Fock with variable-cell geometry optimization and density-of-states analysis is an established non-trivial method. Implementing it correctly demands understanding of crystal structures, basis sets, k-point sampling, and band-structure extraction. Not a textbook operation, but not a novel custom algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves ~5 steps: three sequential CP2K runs (geometry optimization + static DOS for each compound) followed by post-processing of log files to extract lattice constants and DOS at EF. Setting up CP2K inputs with appropriate crystal geometries, basis sets, and job types adds complexity, but I/O is straightforward and steps are largely independent.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves running periodic Hartree-Fock calculations for three molecular crystal systems (pure TCNE, K(TCNE)3, Na(TCNE)3) using CP2K, extracting optimized lattice constants and metallicity. The method is standard quantum chemistry (periodic HF with 6-31G* basis) but requires careful input preparation, handling of crystal symmetry, and interpretation of DOS output. The pipeline is multi-step but not extremely complex. Resources are modest: CPU-only, small memory and data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Three periodic HF calculations on systems of ~30 atoms per cell with 6-31G* basis sets; CPU-only, limited memory footprint, negligible input data.
